subject: chemistry-1
question: Which equation is an example of a decomposition reaction?
explanation:
Decomposition follows the pattern AB -> A + B: a single reactant breaks apart into two or more simpler substances. Hydrogen peroxide breaking down into water and oxygen gas is exactly that pattern. The distractors are a single-replacement reaction (zinc displacing hydrogen from the acid), a combination or synthesis reaction (two elements forming one compound), and a double-replacement precipitation reaction.

ELI-10: Classify by counting what starts and what ends. Decomposition has exactly one starting substance that comes apart into several products. Synthesis is the reverse: several reactants combine into one product. Replacement reactions start with two substances that swap partners. Only the peroxide equation begins with a single compound, so only it is decomposition.
